claims.text: Premelting and melting behavior in HEA nanoparticles is governed primarily by surface segregation of lower-melting-point constituents.
Surface segregation of lower-melting-point constituents reduces local cohesive energy at the nanoparticle surface.
Reduced surface cohesive energy accelerates the onset of premelting.
The nanoparticles can be synthesized with a uniform elemental distribution across each particle.
Controlled sub-melting annealing will induce surface segregation toward lower-melting-point elements.
Enrichment of lower-melting-point elements at the surface lowers surface binding energy.
Lower surface binding energy initiates atomic mobility at lower temperatures.
Surface-segregated nanoparticles will begin premelting at a lower temperature than uniformly distributed control nanoparticles.
The basic melting behavior will remain consistent across the overall composition range despite induced surface segregation.
The proposed mechanism should hold for HEA nanoparticles of similar size and composition under application-relevant heating conditions up to complete melting.
The magnitude of the premelting-temperature reduction may depend on nanoparticle size.
The magnitude of the premelting-temperature reduction may depend on alloy composition.
The magnitude of the premelting-temperature reduction may depend on the degree of surface segregation.
